source.manualTitle: Whirlpool Duet Sport Front-Load Washer (Job Aid L-78)

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the washer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before accessing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.

steps.title: Shipping bolts removed
steps.body: Confirm all shipping bolts are removed. Bolts left installed can cause F25 motor tach faults and no-spin complaints.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove all shipping bolts before operating. Failure to remove shipping bolts can cause motor tach errors.

branches.label: Shipping bolts still installed
branches.oemOutcome: Remove shipping bolts and retest before motor or MCU replacement.

steps.title: Drum turns freely
steps.body: Verify the drum turns freely by hand. Mechanical drag can mimic motor or MCU faults (F25, F31).
steps.sourceExcerpt: Verify the drum turns freely by hand. Mechanical drag can mimic motor or MCU faults (F25, F31).

branches.label: Drum does not turn freely
branches.oemOutcome: Resolve mechanical binding (belt, bearing, foreign object) before electrical motor diagnosis.

steps.title: Disconnect motor 5-wire connector
steps.body: Refer to job aid §4-23 for motor access. Disconnect the 5-wire connector from the drive motor.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to job aid §4-23 for motor access. Disconnect the 5-wire connector from the drive motor.

steps.title: Motor winding resistance at motor connector
steps.body: Set ohmmeter to R×1. Measure between motor pins 1-2, 2-3, and 1-3. Each pair should read approximately 6 Ω on Duet Sport belt-drive motors.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Pins 1 and 2, Pins 2 and 3, Pins 1 and 3 — approximately 6 Ω each.

testPoint.label: Motor winding resistance at motor connector

steps.title: Optional — measure at CCU MS2 (harness path)
steps.body: If fault persists with good motor ohms at the component, disconnect MS2 at the CCU and verify harness continuity to the motor connector. Optional: re-measure motor windings through the harness path.

steps.title: Motor OK — inspect MCU and harness
steps.body: Motor windings measure normal. Inspect motor-to-MCU harness orientation and connections. F28 indicates CCU–MCU serial comm; F06 indicates MCU internal fault. Verify MI3 connector at MCU and belt tension.
steps.sourceExcerpt: F28 CCU–MCU serial comm; F06 MCU internal fault.

steps.title: Reconnect motor harness and restore power
steps.body: Reconnect the 5-wire motor connector. Reassemble panels as needed. Plug in or restore power for Manual Diagnostic Test motor exercise (§6-7).
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect the 5-wire motor connector. Reassemble panels as needed. Plug in or restore power for Manual Diagnostic Test motor exercise (§6-7).

steps.title: Continue to Manual Diagnostic Test
steps.body: You should now be in Diagnostic Test mode (error history reviewed if applicable). Continue below for Manual Diagnostic Test component exercise.
steps.sourceExcerpt: After service history / diagnostic entry, use Manual Diagnostic Test for live component checks (§6-7).

steps.title: Motor runs in Manual Diagnostic Test
steps.body: During Manual Diagnostic Test (§6-7), advance to the wash-speed reversing step (10 min) and spin ramp step. Does the drum reverse at wash speed and ramp to maximum spin?
steps.sourceExcerpt: Drum executes reversing movement at wash speed; drum rotates CCW and ramps to maximum speed.

branches.label: Motor does not run correctly
branches.oemOutcome: Motor ohms good but does not run — suspect MCU, CCU, or harness (F28/F06).

steps.title: Resolve mechanical binding
steps.oemOutcome: Correct belt, bearing, or obstruction before repeating motor test.

steps.title: Replace drive motor
steps.oemOutcome: Replace drive motor when any winding pair is open or out of OEM range.

steps.title: Motor circuit verified
steps.oemOutcome: Motor resistance and live rotation verified — reassemble and verify customer complaint.

steps.title: Suspect MCU/CCU/harness
steps.oemOutcome: Replace MCU or CCU per F06/F28 after confirming motor and harness.
